unit.name: Prompt design, templates, and in-context examples
unit.description: Introduces prompt engineering as the first line of optimization, covering the jagged frontier, centaur/cyborg collaboration styles, specificity, prompt templates, and zero-shot versus few-shot prompting.
unit.summary: Prompt engineering is motivated by a study of consultants where trained AI users performed best within the AI capability frontier, while over-reliance outside the frontier made performance worse [ts=1091s]. The instructor distinguishes centaurs, who divide and delegate tasks to AI, from cyborgs, who integrate AI into continuous back-and-forth work [ts=1204s]. Basic prompt quality improves when the prompt specifies document type, length, audience, focus, and a step-by-step task breakdown [ts=1329s]. Prompt templates are defined as reusable structures with dynamic placeholders that can be embedded in code and personalized from metadata such as role, country, or language [ts=1505s]. The unit then contrasts zero-shot prompting with few-shot prompting, showing how examples can align ambiguous labels such as product-review sentiment without changing model weights [ts=1668s].

key_points.text: AI assistance has a jagged frontier: useful on some tasks, harmful on others when users stop reviewing outputs.
Centaurs divide and delegate between themselves and AI; cyborgs continuously integrate AI into the task flow.
A stronger prompt specifies document type, audience, format, and focus areas instead of asking for a generic summary.
Chain-of-thought style task decomposition asks the model to approach a task step by step and not skip steps.
A prompt template is a predefined structure with placeholders for dynamic inputs.
Few-shot prompting gives examples to align the model to desired style, structure, or task-specific labels.
A prompt can become too long; one engineering workaround is to summarize earlier conversation chapters before continuing.

kp_catalog.name: Jagged AI frontier and centaur/cyborg work styles
kp_catalog.description: The idea that AI helps within a capability frontier but can hurt outside it, and that people collaborate with AI by either delegating chunks or blending AI continuously into work.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The study motivates why prompt-engineering training matters and why users must know when AI is or is not reliable [ts=1142s].

kp_catalog.name: Prompt specificity and stepwise task decomposition
kp_catalog.description: Prompt design principle: specify input type, audience, output format, focus, and task steps to improve controllability and output relevance.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor uses prompt specificity and step-by-step task decomposition as the first practical optimization method before fine-tuning or RAG [ts=1329s].

kp_catalog.name: Prompt templates
kp_catalog.description: Reusable prompt structures with placeholders for dynamic variables that can be embedded in software and personalized at scale.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Prompt templates are tied directly to production scalability and personalization using user metadata [ts=1556s].

kp_catalog.name: In-context learning
kp_catalog.description: Solving a task from examples placed directly in the prompt, without updating model parameters. Task behavior induced by prompts and examples without parameter updates.
